Borrow-lookahead combinational divider
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz, with a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst
path through forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. The four combinational DIV/REM
expressions are the strongest suspect: synthesized long division can
place a carry/borrow chain followed by a remainder-selection mux in each
successive quotient-bit step. Accelerating this local arithmetic path
should improve CoreMark iterations/second without reducing iterations
per cycle. No LESSONS.md exists and log.jsonl contains only the baseline
retest, so there is no earlier divider micro-optimization result.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real-arithmetic DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU operators inside
alu.sv with one shared, purely combinational unsigned quotient/remainder
network whose subtractors use explicit balanced borrow lookahead. Keep
the ALU interface, pipeline registers, instruction latency, forwarding,
memory handshakes and retirement behavior unchanged. This is a local
arithmetic implementation optimization, with no multicycle execution.

Normalize signed DIV/REM operands to unsigned magnitudes, retaining the
operand signs. Starting with the dividend as the residual, process
quotient bits i=31 down to 0. Each step conditionally subtracts divisor
shifted left by i. Implement only the active N=32-i high residual bits,
comparing them against divisor[N-1:0]; reject subtraction when any
divisor bit above N-1 is set. When subtraction fits and produces no
borrow, set quotient[i] and replace the high residual slice with the
difference; otherwise leave the residual unchanged. Preserve the low
i residual bits. At i=0 the residual is the unsigned remainder.

Build each active subtractor from bit generate g=(~x)&y and propagate
p=~(x^y), with borrow-in zero. Combine (g,p) through a balanced prefix
tree, preferably with four-bit local groups and a balanced group tree,
to compute every bit's borrow and the final borrow without a serial
full-width carry chain. Difference bits are x^y^borrow_in. Both the
quotient decision and the selected residual must use these lookahead
results; computing a separate ripple subtraction would retain the
bottleneck. Constant step widths and divisor-overflow checks should
keep the network triangular rather than using 32 full-width rows.

Select quotient versus remainder before the final signed correction.
Negate a signed quotient when operand signs differ; negate a signed
remainder only when the dividend is negative. Preserve exact RV32M
division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results with explicit final overrides.
Keep all RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions unchanged and keep the new
real divider out of that branch. Leave multiplication and base integer
operations untouched. The predicted gain comes from reducing the
borrow dependency repeated across division steps; sharing the four
operations also reduces duplicated arithmetic and routing pressure.

title: Isolate division in a bounded multi-cycle execute unit
motivation:
The baseline's median Fmax is only 5.442 MHz, with a reported 199.837 ns,
156-cell path through forwarding and the EX ALU. alu.sv implements signed
and unsigned division and remainder with combinational / and % operators.
These unrolled arithmetic networks can constrain every instruction's
clock period, even when division is rare. The experiment history contains
only the baseline retest and there is no LESSONS.md or prior structural
attempt. Removing the full-width combinational divider is the strongest
structural opportunity suggested by this timing evidence.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU with one shared, registered radix-2
restoring divider, and interlock the single-issue EX stage around its
request/response handshake. Keep RV32I arithmetic and all multiplication
operations on their existing single-cycle paths. Each ordinary division
performs 32 bounded recurrence cycles, with separate bounded operand
normalization and result sign-correction states if needed. Each recurrence
uses one 33-bit trial subtraction and a borrow-controlled selection, rather
than a chain of 32 division stages. No synthesizable / or % operation may
remain in the normal hardware ALU or divider.

Accept a request exactly once for a valid division instruction when its
forwarded operands are available and older data-memory backpressure permits
launch. Snapshot both forwarded source values and the operation; preserve
those same values for RVFI even after the older forwarding producers drain.
Hold fetch and ID/EX while division is pending. Older MEM/WB instructions
must continue to drain: once EX/MEM has been consumed, inject invalid,
side-effect-free EX/MEM bubbles while the divider runs. Do not freeze an
already accepted store or repeatedly retire the older instruction. Existing
dmem backpressure still holds an unaccepted EX/MEM memory request. Divider
iteration continues independently of bus readiness, and its completed result
remains registered until EX/MEM can accept it exactly once. Release the
front end only on that transfer; the normal EX/MEM forwarding path then
supplies dependent ALU, branch, store and subsequent division instructions.

Use unsigned operand magnitudes for the shared recurrence. Signed quotient
sign is dividend-sign XOR divisor-sign; signed remainder takes the dividend
sign, implementing truncation toward zero. Handle division by zero with an
all-ones quotient and the original dividend remainder, and INT_MIN/-1 with
INT_MIN quotient and zero remainder. Reset cancels pending work. Keep all
decoder legality, misalignment trapping and ordered channel-0-only RVFI
behavior under the existing nret=1 contract.

Preserve the exact existing RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas for all eight
M-extension operations. For division, route the substitute through the same
operand capture, pending-result and consume handshake with a short bounded
latency compatible with the fixed-depth fast formal suite. Real builds must
always use the iterative arithmetic, and real divider correctness and its
full latency must be checked by the existing arithmetic vectors, additional
cocotb coverage and retirement cosimulation. Do not change formal settings,
wrappers, benchmark sources or the fitness harness. Evaluate whether the
Fmax gain outweighs added division cycles using the unchanged stalled
CoreMark run and Gowin median Fmax; the principal uncertainty is dynamic
division frequency and the new limiting multiplier/forwarding path.

title: Small bimodal predictor with targets decoded directly at fetch
motivation:
The baseline has no branch prediction: every aligned taken branch, JAL,
or JALR redirects from EX and discards the younger fetched instruction.
IF/ID is combinational rather than registered, so the fetched instruction
is already available early enough to decode direct control-flow targets
and choose the next fetch PC. CoreMark's repeated loops should benefit
from avoiding these one-cycle bubbles. A small direction-only table avoids
the area and wide read muxes of a tagged branch-target buffer. The measured
critical path passes through forwarding and the combinational M-extension
ALU, so a modest predictor is unlikely to become the limiting timing path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fetch-stage bimodal predictor: 128 two-bit saturating counters,
indexed by PC[8:2] and reset to weakly not taken. Decode the raw fetched
instruction to recognize legal conditional branch funct3 values and JAL.
For a conditional branch, predict taken when its indexed counter's MSB is
set; predict JAL taken unconditionally. Construct B/J immediates directly
from the instruction and add them to the current fetch PC. Predict only
word-aligned targets; use PC+4 for all other instructions, including JALR,
reserved branch encodings, and misaligned direct targets. Do not add a BTB,
return-address stack, global history, cache, or arithmetic redesign.

Carry the exact predicted next PC with each accepted instruction through
IF/ID and ID/EX. Advance the PC to that prediction only when the existing
fetch/decode handshake accepts the instruction. Prediction must not advance
the PC during imem backpressure, load-use interlocks, or dmem backpressure.
In EX retain the existing forwarded operands, branch comparison, target
calculation, jump link value, and misalignment/trap behavior. Compute the
architectural next PC using those existing rules, including PC+4 on a
suppressed misaligned control transfer. Redirect and flush only when a
valid advancing EX instruction's resolved next PC differs from its saved
prediction, rather than on every taken control transfer. Keep the resolved
next PC as the source of RVFI pc_wdata. Correct predictions admit the
fetched successor immediately; incorrect taken, not-taken, or target
predictions recover using the existing one-bubble redirect path.

Train the indexed counter once per valid legal conditional branch accepted
by EX, using its actual taken outcome and saturating at 00/11. Suppress
training during reset, EX hold, bubbles, and branch misalignment traps.
An older dmem stall must hold both prediction metadata and the PC; defer
EX recovery and training until that stall releases, then allow recovery
to override an imem stall or load-use interlock. Comparing the saved
prediction, rather than re-reading a possibly updated counter, preserves
correctness under aliasing and simultaneous predictor lookup/training.

The expected gain is approximately 9 percent in CoreMark iterations per
cycle at similar Fmax, sufficient to exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance
threshold. This is an estimate, not a measured result; counter aliasing,
branch accuracy, and Gowin placement effects are the principal risks.
Preserve nret=1, all decoder legality defaults, exact RVFI order and
retirement behavior, memory handshakes, and the existing correctness gates.

title: Remove redirect-driven instruction masking from the ID critical path
motivation:
The champion's registered divider raised median Fmax to 46.771 MHz and
fitness to 104.12. Its reported worst path now takes 27.303 ns through
forwarding, EX branch recovery, IF instruction masking, load-use control,
and the ID/EX PC register. IF replaces the entire instruction with a NOP
on redirect, so a late forwarded branch decision propagates into source
address comparisons, decode, and register reads. ID also lets flush clear
every payload bit. These dependencies are unnecessary for killing a
younger instruction: its valid and control fields can encode a bubble.
No LESSONS.md exists. The prior micro_opt attempt optimized the old
combinational divider and regressed; that divider is already removed
from the champion. This proposal targets the new measured control path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local optimization to branch-recovery timing: separate bubble
control from the instruction and ID/EX payload datapaths. Preserve the
existing pipeline registers, cycle latency, EX branch resolution, and
single-channel retirement contract. Always expose raw imem_data as the
combinational IF instruction; express redirect or an unavailable fetch
through out.valid rather than a 32-bit instruction-to-NOP mux. Decoding,
register-file addresses, and load-use comparisons must consequently have
no combinational dependency on redirect.

In ID, split updates of payload fields from valid/control updates.
Reset still initializes the complete register. Outside reset, update
PC, operands, immediate, destination/source addresses, and instruction
whenever the existing stall input is low, even if a flush or invalid
fetch will make that captured payload a bubble. Do not put flush or
in.valid in this payload write-enable or select a zero payload on flush.
Give flush priority over stall only for valid and ctrl: flush makes
valid zero and ctrl zero; otherwise a held stage retains both, and an
advancing stage captures in.valid and either the validated decoded
control for a valid instruction or zero control for an invalid fetch.
Thus arbitrary wrong-path payload bits are harmless while every bubble
has mem_read, mem_write, and reg_write cleared. Decoder legality rules
and the is_illegal value of every valid instruction remain unchanged.

Compute load-use comparisons directly from the unmasked fetched source
fields. Qualify the hazard with imem_ready, the existing EX load control,
and nonzero rd, preserving the old unavailable-fetch behavior. Do not
qualify these comparisons with IF valid, flush_if, or redirect: IF valid
includes the late redirect and would recreate the path. A valid EX load
and an EX branch/jump redirect are mutually exclusive under the existing
validated decoder. Keep the current hazard priorities: dmem backpressure
and division wait hold ID/EX; load-use inserts a bubble; an accepted EX
redirect kills the younger instruction and overrides fetch-PC stall,
including imem backpressure. Keep the once-only divider launch/consume
protocol and held MEM/WB forwarding data unchanged.

The expected benefit is higher Fmax at the same useful instruction
latency and approximately unchanged stalled CoreMark cycle count.
Removing the serial redirect-to-instruction-mask-to-hazard dependency
should also lower flush fanout on ID payload flops. Estimate an 18 percent
fitness gain, exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold; this is
unmeasured and another path may become limiting. Validate with the
existing formal and cosim gates, canonical marker-bracketed CoreMark,
and Gowin median Fmax. Do not optimize verification-only RVFI payload
logic or change the harness, wrappers, nret, arithmetic, or bus contract.

title: Register branch recovery at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The current champion scores 104.12 at a median Gowin Fmax of 46.771 MHz.
Its successful structural change replaced combinational division with a
bounded clocked unit; preserve that implementation. The remaining reported
worst path has 50 cells and a 27.303 ns arrival, starting at EX/MEM rd and
ending at ID/EX pc through forwarding, execute, fetch masking, decode and
hazard control. EX currently computes a forwarded branch decision and
immediately feeds it back into the combinational fetch/decode path. This
serial control path, rather than division, is now the strongest measured
structural opportunity. LESSONS.md is absent, and the only previous
structural experiment is the successful iterative divider.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move branch recovery to the registered EX/MEM boundary, while retaining
EX operand forwarding, branch comparisons, target computation, jump link
generation and trap detection. Replace the combinational EX-to-front-end
redirect with a redirect derived exclusively from registered EX/MEM
fields: a valid legal taken branch or jump, with its registered resolved
pc_next as the target. Existing branch_taken, ctrl.is_jump, ctrl.is_illegal,
valid and pc_next fields are sufficient; no new pipeline stage or retirement
channel is required. Do not let live EX operands, comparisons, target
adders or div_wait participate in this registered redirect's assertion or
target selection. The timing benefit comes from separating forwarded
branch resolution from PC, fetch masking and ID/EX control by a register.

In the recovery cycle, let the resolving EX/MEM branch or jump advance
normally into MEM/WB and retire exactly once. Simultaneously redirect the
fetch PC, invalidate the fetched instruction, clear the younger ID/EX
instruction, and insert a fully cleared, side-effect-free EX/MEM bubble
instead of accepting that younger instruction's EX result. This last kill
is essential: delayed recovery must prevent a wrong-path load, store,
register write or second control transfer from reaching MEM. Preserve the
branch/jump's own PC+4 link result and exact RVFI source values and next PC.
Not-taken branches continue without recovery. Misaligned branch/jump traps
retain the existing suppressed redirect, PC+4 next PC and disabled writeback.

Recovery has priority over younger load-use and division holds and over
instruction-bus backpressure. Derive it from valid accepted EX/MEM control
transfers, never from a bubble or an unaccepted EX instruction. Genuine
older dmem backpressure must still hold EX/MEM and ID/EX until accepted;
branches have no dmem transaction, so low dmemReady alone must not postpone

saturating direction counter and an unconditional-jump bit per entry.
Fetch lookup uses only the registered PC and stored predictor state;
neither instruction-memory data nor a B/J immediate adder participates
in selecting the predicted target. A matching conditional entry predicts
taken when its counter MSB is set, and a matching JAL/JALR entry always
predicts its last resolved target. A miss predicts PC+4. This is one small
target-and-direction predictor, without global history or a return stack.

title: Share one native DSP multiplier across RV32M signedness variants
motivation:
The champion scores 117.38 at a median 49.269 MHz. Its worst path is
26.661 ns through register-file reads, operand muxes, the EX multiplier
and result selection. A fresh Gowin build reproduced the reported
place-option-0 Fmax of 46.803 MHz and explicitly identified a 3.780 ns
multiplier cell on that path. alu.sv computes three independent
full-width products for signed/signed, unsigned/unsigned and
signed/unsigned variants, and the timed design consumes six DSP blocks.

and product-selection logic without adding an instruction cycle.

regressed, while redirect-mask removal gained only 3.63 percent and
is already incorporated into the champion's predictor recovery.

motivation:
The champion scores 117.38 at 49.269 MHz and 4197447 bracketed CoreMark
cycles. Its worst reported path is 26.661 ns through register-file/ID,
EX and u_alu to the memory interface. The successful structural divider
isolation removed a much deeper arithmetic path; the later registered
branch-recovery attempt instead lost throughput with almost no Fmax
gain. There is no LESSONS.md. Multiplication is the remaining large
combinational arithmetic network in alu.sv, including three signedness
variants. A fresh make timing TARGET=bench run reproduces placement-0
Fmax 46.803 MHz and the 26.661 ns worst path. Its detailed arrival path
passes through u_alu/mult_5_s1/B[12] to DOUT[36], a 3.780 ns DSP arc,
between operand muxes and result-selection logic. This confirms that
multiplication participates in the limiting path. Separating forwarded
operands, DSP products and result assembly with real registers is the
most promising next structural cut; the score still uses median Fmax.

with both stall flags reproduces 4197447 cycles between marker
retirements, with 2922015 instructions and 93960 MUL retirements. No
high-half multiply or DIV/REM retires inside that bracket. Thus a short
low-half completion path matters much more than high-half throughput.

Replace the combinational MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU datapaths with one
bounded, clocked multiplier using four registered unsigned 16x16 partial
products. Keep the present branch predictor, recovery point, RV32I
single-cycle path, iterative divider and nret=1 contract. This proposal
changes only multiplication execution structure and its necessary
interlock; it does not add a pipeline stage to ordinary instructions.

A launch edge captures the two fully forwarded 32-bit operands and op.
On the following edge register p00=a[15:0]*b[15:0],
p01=a[15:0]*b[31:16], p10=a[31:16]*b[15:0], and
p11=a[31:16]*b[31:16], each a 32-bit unsigned product. Use inferred
DSP-sized products without device-specific primitives, so the same RTL
remains usable by Verilator and riscv-formal. Do not leave any full-width
combinational multiplier connected to the ordinary ALU result mux.

Recombine through registered, at-most-33-bit arithmetic stages rather
than a cascade of full-width products and adders. First register
cross={1'b0,p01}+{1'b0,p10}. Next register
low_sum={1'b0,p00}+{1'b0,cross[15:0],16'b0} and
upper_base={1'b0,p11}+{16'b0,cross[32:16]}.
The unsigned low half is low_sum[31:0] and unsigned high half is
upper_base[31:0]+zero_extend(low_sum[32]). Reuse the registered
low_sum carry in high-half assembly. Signed-high correction follows
the identity high_signed=high_unsigned-(a_signed && a[31] ? b : 0)
-(b_signed && b[31] ? a : 0), modulo 2^32. MULH marks both operands
signed, MULHSU only a, and MULHU neither; MUL always uses the unsigned
low half. Keep the two possible high-half subtractions on separate
bounded registered steps, bypassing unnecessary correction steps for
MUL/MULHU and nonnegative operands. Each state transition is explicit,
no request depends on symbolic operands eventually becoming ready, and
worst-case real completion has a fixed small bound. Give low-half MUL a
shorter completion path: on the edge immediately after partial-product
capture, register result={sum18[15:0],p00[15:0]} and enter COMPLETE,
where sum18=zero_extend(p00[31:16])+zero_extend(p01[15:0])
+zero_extend(p10[15:0]). Only two narrow additions follow the DSP product
registers on this path; it skips the cross/high-assembly states. Use
explicit 18-bit sum operands and truncate only the final upper result
half. MUL therefore adds three held EX cycles (operand launch, product
capture, result capture), then transfers on the following edge. High
variants use the bounded registered reconstruction above; at most eight
edges from launch to done suffice even with both corrections. Completion
stays sticky until EX consumes it exactly once. Reset cancels work.

Mirror the divider's established transaction discipline. Launch a valid
multiply once when older data-memory backpressure permits it; snapshot
raw forwarded rs1/rs2 for RVFI as well as arithmetic. Hold PC and ID/EX
while multiplication is pending. Older MEM/WB instructions drain and
a consumed EX/MEM instruction is replaced by a fully invalid,
side-effect-free bubble; hold only an unaccepted older memory request.
Internal multiplier progress is independent of memory ready, and a
completed result cannot be overwritten during backpressure. Release the
front end only when EX/MEM accepts the product. The normal EX/MEM result
then forwards to dependent ALU, branch, JALR, store, division and
multiplication instructions. Gate predictor training and recovery on
actual EX acceptance, retaining current mismatch recovery and all trap
rules. Do not issue or retire younger instructions out of order.

Retain the exact four multiplication RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and
route them through the same captured-operand, sticky-completion and
consume protocol with a short bounded latency suitable for the existing
fixed-depth formal gate. Preserve the current divider's real arithmetic,
ALTOPS behavior and handshake. Real builds must exercise the registered
partial products, all signed-high corrections and low-half overflow.

Three added held cycles for the measured 93960 low-half multiplies
imply 281880 extra cycles, approximately 6.72 percent of the current
bracket, before accounting for overlaps and changed stall alignment.

acceptance margin, and about 63.1 MHz yields the expected 20 percent

implementation_notes:
# Registered partial-product multiplier

Implemented the hypothesis in `cores/bench/rtl/` and extended only the two
corresponding `cores/bench/test/test_*.py` files. This requested notes file
is at the worktree root for the orchestrator's notes reader.

## Implementation

- Added `multiplier.sv` with captured operands/op, four registered unsigned
  16x16 products, and sticky completion until consume. Reset cancels work.
- MUL captures its result directly from two explicit 18-bit additions after
  the product registers. It holds EX for three cycles and transfers on the
  fourth edge, as proposed.
- High variants register the 33-bit cross sum, low sum and upper base, then
  reuse the low-sum carry for unsigned high assembly. Signed corrections
  subtract each required operand in separate registered 32-bit steps;
  unnecessary corrections are bypassed. Completion takes five through seven
  edges including launch, within the requested eight-edge bound.
- Removed all combinational full-width multiply networks from `alu.sv`.
  All four exact multiplication ALTOPS formulas now use captured operands
  and the same sticky handshake, completing on the edge after launch.
- Generalized the existing division wait to `m_wait`. Launch waits for
  older memory acceptance; PC and ID/EX hold; older stages drain; consumed
  EX/MEM contents become a completely zeroed bubble. Both units progress
  independently of bus ready. Raw forwarded RVFI operands are captured at
  launch in shared M-operation snapshot registers. Prediction training and
  recovery remain qualified by actual EX acceptance.
- Preserved divider RTL/arithmetic/ALTOPS, branch predictor/recovery,
  decoder/trap rules, ordinary instruction latency, memory protocol,
  retirement ordering and the nret=1 top-level contract.

The only implementation deviations are sharing the existing RVFI source
snapshots between multiplication and division, and completing the worst
high-half case in seven rather than eight launch-inclusive edges. No
evaluation, wrapper, benchmark source, or configuration files were changed.

- Required Verilator lint: PASS with no warnings. ALTOPS lint also PASS.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  PASS, 53 checks, zero failures, first attempt; no fixes/retries required.
- `make test TARGET=bench`: PASS, all six existing unit-test runners.
  Multiplier tests preserve every prior result assertion and divider vector,
  add exact signed/unsigned boundary and seeded random products, partial
  carries/overflow, busy input changes, retained completion, consecutive
  requests and reset in every real execution state.

  DIV-to-MUL, dependent consecutive MULs, every high variant, x0, reset,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the predictor with one compact 16-entry direct-mapped tagged
target/direction table and carry its exact taken target as an 18-bit
word address. This is one predictor-footprint optimization: trade a
modest increase in target conflicts for smaller tables, simpler lookup
selection and narrower metadata routing. Keep PC-only asynchronous
lookup, two-bit bimodal counters, unconditional JAL/JALR entries and the
champion's EX recovery protocol. Do not change pipeline depth, arithmetic,
retirement width, memory handshakes or the recovery penalty.

Use the same four-bit hash for lookup and update:
index = PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6]. Store tag PC[19:6] (14 bits), target[19:2]
(18 bits), the two-bit counter and jump bit in 16-row arrays. Keep a
separate 16-bit valid bitmap, reset only that bitmap, and leave payload
arrays unreset for memory inference. A tag match plus equal hash index
uniquely identifies all aligned PC bits within the lower 1 MiB: the
stored tag includes the high hash operand, so equality also implies
equality of PC[5:2]. Retain the current PC[31:20]==0, PC[1:0]==0 and
target range/alignment guards. Never truncate a PC or target before its
guard. No extra pipeline stage, additional read/write port or lookup
dependence on instruction-memory data is introduced.

Preserve every existing update rule with the new dimensions and tag:
allocate only EX-accepted legal representable branches/jumps, initialize
replacement conditional counters weakly according to outcome, saturate
matching conditional counters, and overwrite actual JAL/JALR targets.
A jump-to-conditional kind change starts weak. Ordinary, illegal,
trapping and unrepresentable updates invalidate only their matching tag;
unrelated tags survive. Lookup accepted on an update edge uses pre-edge
state. Holds and divider waits must not repeat training. The hash changes
collision policy, never architectural instruction or trap semantics.

fetch is masked. Do not emit next_pc or PC+4 into this field on a
not-taken prediction; EX does not use its target in that case. Keep the
existing full-width next_pc selection and PC register. ID's existing
typed assignment carries the smaller target with the same instruction,
and retains or clears it on exactly the existing hold/flush edges.

In EX reconstruct the saved target as {12'b0, in.predicted_target, 2'b0}
for comparison against the full 32-bit actual_target. Retain separate
direction and taken-target mismatch checks, acceptance gating and the
full-width architectural redirect target. Compare all actual target
bits, so a changed indirect target outside the representable range or
stale modified instruction still recovers correctly. Keep current
illegal/misaligned suppression, RVFI resolved next PCs, synchronous
wrong-path killing and recovery priority over front-end stalls.

multicycle multiplication and predictor shrinking did not beat the

title: Register one unsigned DSP product before RV32M result selection
motivation:
The champion scores 170.74 iter/sec at median Gowin Fmax 71.668 MHz
with 4,197,447 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent.

branch predictor, direct accepted-EX recovery, iterative divider and

Instantiate a dedicated clocked multiplier. On the first eligible EX
edge of a valid MUL, MULH, MULHU or MULHSU, capture product_q <= a * b
as an unsigned 32x32-to-64-bit native multiplication. Capture operation
and raw source operands on the same edge for high-half correction and

All four operations share this unsigned product; no opcode-controlled
sign extension or signedness selection may precede its DSP inputs.
Remove the signed 33x33 combinational product from the ordinary ALU.
Add neither a preliminary operand-capture cycle nor a separately
registered final low-half result: existing ID/EX and EX/MEM provide
the operand launch and final result capture boundaries.

For MUL, assert ready immediately after the product-capture edge and
expose product_q[31:0]. The next accepted EX/MEM edge captures the value
and releases ID/EX. MUL therefore adds exactly one held EX cycle when
older memory backpressure is absent. Its completion path contains
registered-product selection without partial-product assembly adders.
Retain product_q and readiness until consumption, including through
dmem stalls. Reset cancels work by clearing control/valid state; an
uninitialized product must never be exposed as a valid result.

For high-half operations use the identity
high_result = product_q[63:32]

              - (signed_b && b_q[31] ? a_q : 0), modulo 2^32.

these two states stay off the MUL fast path. Ready high results remain
registered until consumed. All real operations become ready within

an all-zero, side-effect-free bubble while EX waits. Genuine dmem stalls
retain the unaccepted older request. Internal arithmetic progresses
independently of memory readiness. Consume completion exactly once
and return idle on that edge so a consecutive multiply can launch in

title: Train the predictor from registered EX/MEM control-flow results
motivation:
The champion reaches 170.74 iter/sec with median Fmax 71.668 MHz and
4197447 stalled CoreMark bracket cycles. Its current predictor trains
directly from combinational EX outcome, target, trap and acceptance logic.
Updates therefore fan out from EX into tag, target, direction and validity
storage on the same edge that resolves the control transfer. The existing
EX/MEM bundle already registers the PC, controls, outcome, branch target
and architectural next PC needed for training.

No LESSONS.md exists. Prior capacity reduction and target banking did not
beat the latest champion. A baseline reproduction passed canonical CRCs,
bounds and completion with exactly 4197447 bracket cycles. Sequential
replay counted only 62551 predictor misses in 2922016 timed retirements;
a small history predictor and return stack removed fewer than 2000 each.

reached only 72.212 MHz, below acceptance, with 7424 logic cells and 3841
registers. Its timing reports expose long EX-to-predictor update paths.
Registered predictor feedback is a distinct way to shorten those paths
without increasing target capacity, adding broad flop tables or relying
on a large accuracy gain. The champion's ALU remains a competing limit.

title: Balanced four-bit branch comparison shortens EX feedback
motivation:
The champion scores 184.91 iter/sec at 77.615 MHz with 4197447
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
ID/EX rs2_val bit zero and crosses EX, predictor logic and ID in
19.133 ns over 38 cells. A low operand bit reaching branch feedback
is consistent with a long carry-chain magnitude comparison. The
current EX directly expresses full-width signed and unsigned less
than and greater than or equal comparisons. A shallow comparison
network can shorten this operand-to-control dependency without
changing prediction accuracy or instruction latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX's full-width branch magnitude comparisons with one shared
balanced lexicographic comparator. Divide both finalized 32-bit
ID/EX operands into eight four-bit groups. For each group compute
unsigned less-than and equality. Combine adjacent groups in a fixed
three-level tree, always treating the more significant group as H:
lt_pair = lt_H OR (eq_H AND lt_L), eq_pair = eq_H AND eq_L.
The root supplies exact unsigned less-than and equality. Use explicit
constant-index intermediate wires so this remains a bounded local
network rather than a serial fold or another full-width subtractor.
No group comparison is wider than four bits.

Reproduce the measured topology with wire [15:1] compare_lt and
compare_eq. For generate index g=0..7, assign compare_lt[8+g] =
rs1[4*g +: 4] < rs2[4*g +: 4] and compare_eq[8+g] =
rs1[4*g +: 4] == rs2[4*g +: 4]. For g=1..7, assign compare_lt[g] =
compare_lt[2*g+1] | (compare_eq[2*g+1] & compare_lt[2*g]) and
compare_eq[g] = compare_eq[2*g+1] & compare_eq[2*g]. This heap places
lower bits on even children and higher bits on odd children. Root
index one is the full-word comparison. Signed less-than is explicitly
(rs1[31] ^ rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : compare_lt[1].

Signed less-than is operand A's sign when the operand signs differ,
and the root unsigned less-than otherwise. BEQ uses root equality,
BNE its inverse, BLT signed less-than, BGE its inverse, BLTU unsigned
less-than and BGEU its inverse. Preserve the default branch_cond=0
for reserved branch operation encodings. Compute all comparisons from
in.rs1_val and in.rs2_val, which are already finalized and stable.
Do not use subtraction-result sign alone for signed comparison.

Keep the same EX acceptance, branch_taken qualification, target
arithmetic, alignment traps, immediate redirect, predicted-metadata
comparison, once-only predictor update and ID forwarding behavior.
Predictor policy, capacity, storage and update visibility are unchanged.
Pipeline registers, stages, instruction latency, memory handshakes,
division and multiplication, ALTOPS formulas, decoder legality and
the nret=1 IO/RVFI contract remain unchanged. This is one branch
comparator micro-optimization, not a predictor or pipeline redesign.

An isolated RTL prototype of exactly this four-bit topology measures
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at 81.911, 81.537 and 81.537 MHz,
median 81.537 MHz versus the champion's 77.615 MHz. Resources are
4618 logic cells, 1857 registers, 32 LUT-RAM units, five BSRAMs and
two DSPs. The previous 38-cell EX/predictor/ID comparison path is
absent from the reported worst paths; EX ALU forwarding and ID
operand capture become the limiting paths. A narrower two-bit-group
comparator reached only 71.331 MHz in placement option one; retain
the measured four-bit topology rather than shrinking its groups.

The prototype passes the existing pipeline suite and additional
boundary/random coverage: all 32 cocotb pipeline tests pass. The new
test checks all six branch predicates for 181 operand pairs with and
without both bus stalls, including each bit boundary, competing
significant groups, sign extremes, equal operands and seeded random
values, checking exact RVFI sources and next PCs and accepted stores.
A combinational SAT miter proves unsigned less-than, equality and
signed less-than equivalent to the original operators for all 64
input bits. This is an arithmetic equivalence proof, not a timing
measurement. Strict Verilator lint passes in real-arithmetic and
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS modes. All 53 unchanged nret=1 fast formal checks
pass using an isolated framework copy with the original wrapper_si.sv
and checks_si.cfg, unchanged properties and unchanged depths.
All eight unchanged retirement cosim runs pass for
selftest and random1/2/3 with and without bus stalls. The unchanged
canonical 2K CoreMark run passes CRC/UART completion, memory bounds
and start/stop-marker validation and retains exactly 4197447 bracket

Median vendor Fmax times this measured iterations/cycle gives

Introduce one elastic fetch/decode register and move instruction decoding
and immediate generation before it. The registered transaction contains
PC, original instruction, decoded ctrl_t, immediate, prediction metadata
and validity. Decode the actual imemData with the existing strict decoder;
its is_illegal default and positively validated opcode/funct matches stay
unchanged. The following operand-collection stage reads only this saved
instruction and saved control/immediate fields, rather than decoding
live instruction-memory data again. There must be no empty-slot bypass
from imemData into register addresses or execute-operand capture.

The operand stage retains current youngest EX > MEM > RF forwarding and
WB write-first behavior. It captures finalized raw rs1/rs2 for branches,
stores, multiplication and RVFI. Also capture the general ALU inputs on
the same ID/EX acceptance: alu_a is the saved PC for AUIPC, otherwise
finalized rs1; alu_b is the saved immediate for immediate operations,
otherwise finalized rs2. EX consumes these two operand flops directly,
with no late alu_src or is_auipc mux. Keep the existing independently
prepared native multiplier inputs from raw rs1/rs2 and registered sign
bits. Thus decode, register access and execution operand selection are
partitioned across the new fetch/decode and existing execute boundaries;
this is one pipeline-topology change, not a collection of predictor or
arithmetic-unit redesigns.

Use a one-entry elastic decoded-instruction slot. Fill only when imemReady
is high and the slot is empty or the current head is genuinely consumed.
Advance the fetch PC exactly on fill. Permit simultaneous consume/refill
for one-instruction-per-cycle steady-state throughput and permit an empty
slot to fill during an operand-stage hold. A full unconsumed slot retains
all control, instruction, PC, immediate and prediction fields. A missing
new instruction-memory response must not erase the buffered instruction
or prevent its decode/operand-stage consumption.

Derive head consumption from its validity and actual ID/EX acceptance.
Do not pop on a load-use bubble, division wait, older data-memory hold,
reset or recovery. Compute load-use against the saved source fields and
preserve the one-cycle load-to-use interlock and current-MEM load bypass.
Data-memory stalls retain the current request and finalized held operands;
older MEM/WB drains with the existing validity discipline. Do not add an
extra result stage or a general register-dependency bubble.

Keep immediate accepted-EX branch recovery and predictor training. On
redirect, synchronously clear the decoded slot and ID/EX, discard the
incoming wrong-path transaction and set the fetch PC to the resolved
destination even under imem backpressure or a full slot. Genuine EX holds
still suppress recovery at its source. The target instruction must enter
through the new register on a later ready edge. Save the prediction used
on the original fetch acceptance and retain it unchanged through holds;
subsequent predictor training must not rewrite buffered metadata. Reset

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one synchronous next-PC lookahead target predictor, retaining
exactly the existing 64 direct-mapped entries and prediction policy.
Partition target storage into four 16-word, 18-bit banks indexed by
PC[7:6], with PC[5:2] selecting a row. Use constant bank instances and
small unreset arrays, with an enabled synchronous read register per bank
and a registered bank selector. Read all four banks at the selected row
on a lookup advance, then select the registered target with a balanced
four-input mux. This is approximately 1152 target-memory bits plus 72
read-register bits, not a broad flop replacement or additional capacity.
Target storage should infer shallow distributed LUT memory rather than
an asynchronous 64-word BSRAM plus fabric output qualification. Keep the
current tag, valid, jump and counter storage organization unless a small
indexing adjustment is necessary to address the same logical row.

Predictor outputs are registered and describe the current fetch PC;
the lookup address describes the normal selected next PC. In IF compute
next_pc from the current registered prediction, choosing its target when
taken and PC+4 otherwise. On an ordinary accepted fetch edge, advance PC
to next_pc and register the bank reads, bank selector and direction for
that same address. The following cycle then already has both its PC and
prediction. Lookup must never depend on its own unregistered direction
or target output. Preserve one accepted fetch per cycle with one logical
lookup port; do not add an instruction pipeline stage or a fetch queue.

Add lookup_advance and lookup_clear controls. lookup_advance is
!reset && !redirect && !stall_if. Hold every registered prediction field
together with PC under imem backpressure, load-use interlocks, dmem holds
and division waits. Register direction from the existing PC range and
alignment guards, valid bit, tag match and jump-or-counter-MSB policy.
Keep tag-hit, valid, reset and miss-to-zero multiplexers outside the raw
bank read-register inputs. Read payload and bank selector need not reset:
reset clears table validity and registered predicted_taken, which makes
unknown payload harmless. Reconstruct targets with twelve zero upper bits
and two zero alignment bits. When direction is false, raw target payload
must have no effect on PC, validity, architectural state or RVFI.

Accepted EX recovery still immediately writes redirect_target to PC and
overrides every front-end stall. On that edge lookup_clear clears direction,
lookup_advance is false and target payload may hold. Conservatively predict
sequentially for the first fetch after reset/recovery, then prime the next
lookahead on normal acceptance. Never place a lookup of combinational
redirect_target after the EX target adder. This may add a few cold misses
but cannot delay architectural recovery. Capture exact prediction metadata
with each instruction and retain it through every ID/EX hold.

Training stays at the existing once-per-valid-EX-acceptance boundary.
Only the addressed target bank writes; read/update at the same edge uses
the old row in RTL. Preserve saturation, weak replacement initialization,
unconditional jump behavior, changing indirect targets, jump-to-branch
reinitialization, target range/alignment guards and matching-only stale
invalidation. Not-taken branches train their direct destination, never
PC+4. Predictor state remains advisory and EX independently resolves all
architectural outcomes and full-width targets, including stale hits.

Factor predictor control-flow eligibility independently of branch outcome
to prevent a resolved comparator from feeding trap logic before predictor
resolution. branch_eligible is decoded legal branch AND aligned destination;
jump_eligible is decoded legal jump AND aligned destination. actual_taken is

target inequality can be checked without actual_taken gating, because
direction mismatch already recovers when actual_taken is false. Predictor
allocation may reject an unaligned branch destination regardless of outcome,

architectural trap/next-PC behavior. Remove branch-trap outcome from unrelated
EX producer gating while retaining decoded reg_write, decoded legality and
jump-alignment suppression: decoded branches never write rd. Preserve
forwarding priority, arithmetic and all instruction-stage boundaries.

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only the register-file storage topology: replace the 31 large
resettable flop words with four independent eight-row asynchronous
distributed-memory banks, replicated once for each read port. Bank
index is address[4:3], local row is address[2:0]. Each bank owns two
unreset logic [31:0] arrays [0:7], one for rs1 and one for rs2, with
asynchronous indexed reads and identical synchronous writes. Read
every bank's selected local row, then select the addressed bank with
a shallow four-input mux. Use portable inferred memories, not vendor
primitives, and never introduce a synchronous read or another stage.

Each bank's write enable is !reset && w_en && w_addr != 0 and a sized
equality between w_addr[4:3] and its constant bank number. Both copies
receive w_data at w_addr[2:0] on the same edge. Arrays have no reset,
initialization loop or per-row constant-index flop coding. Maintain
a separate 32-bit written/valid bitmap: synchronous reset clears it,
a nonzero accepted write sets the corresponding bit, and bit zero
remains clear. Reads of unwritten registers return zero, preserving
the current reset-clears-all observable behavior even across repeated
resets with populated memories. Reset inhibits both payload writes
and validity updates. Invalid raw memory bits must never affect a
read result, execution, memory side effect or valid RVFI transaction.

Preserve the current combinational read contract and priority exactly:
address zero returns zero; otherwise matching w_en/w_addr returns
w_data in the same cycle; otherwise a written address returns the
selected asynchronous bank word; otherwise return zero. Write-first
bypass applies to both ports, including simultaneous collisions.
Keep its current behavior during an asserted reset before the reset
edge; synchronous reset wins over committing a pending write.

The essential structural condition is that shallow payload memories
map to distributed LUT RAM with asynchronous outputs. Gowin must not
map these arrays into synchronous BSRAM or absorb the existing ID/EX
operand registers into memory read registers. Inspect synthesis and
timing reports to confirm real finalized operand flops still launch
native multiplier and branch execution. The two copies provide two
independent combinational read addresses without a multiport flop
mux. Smaller local memories reduce register-data routing and free
nearly a thousand storage flops without changing instruction latency,
predictor accuracy or dependency scheduling.

Keep ID's youngest EX > MEM > RF forwarding and RF's WB write-first
behavior, all finalized operand and multiplier sign flops, and every
stall/flush acceptance rule. Captured EX operands remain stable while
older producers drain. Leave pipeline depth, load-use interlock, native
multiplier, iterative divider, predictor, immediate EX recovery and
memory handshake untouched. Preserve nret=1 and the exact top-level
memory/RVFI port set, decoder legality, traps, order, bounds, true
RV32IM arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas and all hard invariants. Change only
allowed RTL and cocotb tests; do not modify evaluation-contract files.

An isolated prototype of this exact four-bank topology measures Gowin
placement options 0/1/2 at 82.333, 82.428 and 82.428 MHz, median 82.428
MHz. Resources are 3766 logic cells, 896 registers, 96 LUT-RAM units,
five BSRAMs and two DSPs. Compared with the champion, 961 registers
and 852 logic cells disappear; the additional 64 LUT-RAM units store
the replicated register-file banks. BSRAM and DSP counts are unchanged.
Timing starts from finalized ID/EX operands, confirming preservation
of the execute launch boundary. The remaining placement-1 worst path
crosses general ALU input selection, addition and EX-to-ID forwarding.

Strict lint passes in real arithmetic and ALTOPS modes. All seven
existing register-file tests and all 34 existing pipeline tests pass.
All eight unchanged retirement cosim runs pass: selftest and random1,
random2 and random3, each with and without both bus stalls. Canonical
stalled CoreMark passes completion, all CRC/UART validation, memory
bounds and timing-marker checks with exactly 4,197,447 bracket cycles.
At the time of this proposal, 52 of 53 unchanged nret=1 formal checks
pass in an isolated copy of the original framework; reg_ch0 is still
solving, so full formal correctness is not claimed. No original formal
source, wrapper, property, configuration or depth has been changed.

Median vendor Fmax times actual iterations/cycle gives approximately
196.3765 iter/sec, a 1.09 percent gain over 194.25. Predict an integer
one percent fitness improvement with medium confidence. This measured
prototype is below the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold and is not a
demonstrated champion replacement. At unchanged cycles, median Fmax
must exceed about 85.29 MHz and fitness must exceed 203.1855 iter/sec
to clear that gate. Smaller gains must not be accepted as a win.

The four-bank storage topology is the strongest isolated structural
option found in this investigation. Two sixteen-row banks, eight
four-row banks, alternate bank indexing and folding validity/write
bypass into masked bank terms all timed worse. Moving RF commit earlier or preparing general ALU
operands earlier also timed worse. Retain the specified four-bank
asynchronous layout rather than combining those unsuccessful changes.
Extra read replication, bank-output muxes, valid-bit qualification,
the remaining EX-to-ID path and the unfinished register-state proof
are the practical limits. Final implementation must complete every
unchanged correctness gate and obtain fresh median vendor timing and
canonical stalled marker-bracketed throughput. A timing or area gain
without those checks is insufficient.

title: Recover predicted control flow from a registered EX/MEM decision
motivation:
The champion reaches 194.25 iterations/sec at 81.537 MHz with 4197447
canonical stalled CoreMark bracket cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Earlier
structural experiments added decode or multiply stages without winning;
changing register-file storage gave only 1.10 percent. The round-2
registered-recovery experiment lost throughput when every taken transfer
required recovery, before the present tagged predictor existed. With
prediction, recovery happens only on a mismatch: prior replay counted
approximately 62551 misses, giving about 1.5 percent first-order cost
for an additional recovery bubble. This makes a registered recovery
boundary a materially different tradeoff on the current champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

In EX independently resolve the actual direction, full-width target,
alignment traps and architectural next PC exactly as today. Register

instruction in EX/MEM. Its registered pc_next is the recovery address.

recovery assertion or target. This is one structural retiming of the

insufficient because an extra younger instruction is already in EX.
Suppress that younger instruction's predictor training, divider launch
and consume, and EX acceptance. Recovery overrides younger load-use,
division and instruction-bus holds. An actual unaccepted older data
request still holds EX/MEM until dmemReady; recover only when it accepts.
This also handles a stale predicted ordinary LOAD/STORE or a trapping
instruction, rather than assuming every recovery comes from a branch.

Keep predictor training at the existing accepted EX boundary, including
ordinary/stale invalidations. Keep the exact 64-entry tagged predictor,
counter policy, target guards, asynchronous lookup and old-row behavior.
Retain the prediction saved at fetch; delayed recovery must still repair
changing JALR targets, stale ordinary hits and illegal/misaligned taken
predictions. Only surviving EX instructions train once. Reset clears
pending recovery. Preserve the resolving instruction's architectural
PC/link/result, memory transaction and RVFI source values.

native shared multiplier, balanced branch comparator and sticky iterative

ALTOPS formulas, decoder default-illegal checks, traps, memory bounds,
nret=1 and the exact top-level IO, strict retirement order, progress,
canonical CRCs and marker brackets. Change no evaluation-contract file.

Predict an eight percent fitness gain with low confidence: a roughly

operand capture can still dominate. At a 1.5 percent cycle increase,
median Fmax must exceed approximately 86.57 MHz to clear 203.1855

title: Predecoded 40-bit predictor training transaction
motivation:
EX currently feeds resolved legality, direction and target directly into
the predictor's tagged counter read-modify-write and table write enables.
Several historical critical paths cross EX and this maintenance logic.
Prior direct-target registration and ID prevalidation did not clear the
acceptance margin; EX/MEM-consumption training gained only 1.51 percent
against its then-champion. A dedicated compact transaction can isolate
table maintenance without retaining architectural EX/MEM fields or
depending on MEM readiness. Accuracy alone has limited headroom here:
a CoreMark architectural trace found approximately 62551 BTB misses,
and an eight-entry return stack removed only 1194 of them.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert one predecoded, 40-bit training register inside branch_predictor.
Retain the exact 64-entry tagged BTB, original two-bit direction counters,
jump policy, target memories, asynchronous PC-only lookup and immediate
EX recovery. This is one predictor-maintenance pipeline change; do not
change table capacity, prediction metadata, instruction stages, arithmetic
or branch-resolution logic.

Capture PC[19:2] and target[19:2] as two 18-bit payloads plus three bits:
allocate, jump kind and actual taken. The fortieth bit is transaction
validity. On every nonreset edge assign validity from update_en AND the
full original PC range/alignment guard, PC[31:20]==0 and PC[1:0]==0.
Capture payload when update_en is asserted. Predecode allocate from the
original effective EX legality, branch-or-jump kind and full target
guard, target[31:20]==0 and target[1:0]==0. Save jump kind and actual
outcome separately. Check both full addresses before compressed fields
can authorize a table write; invalid PC updates remain inert, and invalid
target or illegal/ordinary updates retain matching-only invalidation.

Reset clears transaction validity and the existing table-valid bitmap,
cancelling pending work. Leave transaction payload and memory payload
unreset, guarded by validity. The input acceptance strobe is unchanged:
one valid, advancing EX instruction, with reset, dmem hold and division
wait excluded. A previously captured transaction applies once on the
following edge even if a later EX instruction is now held. Validity is
replaced every edge, so bubbles cannot repeat a write. One transaction
per edge matches nret=1 throughput and requires no ready signal or queue
interlock.

Derive maintenance index from captured PC[5:0] and tag from PC[17:6],
exactly corresponding to the original PC[7:2] and PC[19:8]. Perform
tag-hit comparison, counter read/selection, saturation, replacement,
kind changes and table write decoding entirely after this register.
Allocate when saved allocate is true; otherwise invalidate only a saved
PC's matching tag. Conditional replacement starts weak according to its
saved actual outcome, matching conditional counters saturate, and a
jump-to-branch replacement starts weak. JAL/JALR write the saved actual
target and unconditional kind. A not-taken branch retains its direct
destination for target training, never PC+4. Back-to-back transactions
apply in original order, including repeated PCs and conflicting tags.

Keep read-before-write lookup behavior: lookup and instruction acceptance
on an application edge see the old row. Add no EX-to-fetch write-through
bypass. Each instruction still retains its exact accepted prediction;
EX independently resolves full architectural direction/target and
recovers immediately on a mismatch. The added training edge can produce
another cold miss for very short loops, but cannot change execution.
Preserve synchronous wrong-path killing and recovery priority over
front-end stalls, stale-code repair, changing JALR targets, misalignment
and illegal traps, nret=1/top-level IO, all RVFI PC/link/order semantics,
decoder default legality, true and ALTOPS arithmetic, memory handshakes
and bounds, canonical CRCs and marker bracketing. Modify no eval files.

An isolated prototype of this exact transaction measured Gowin Fmax
78.350, 82.988 and 82.988 MHz across placement options 0/1/2: median
82.988 MHz, 4590 LUTs, 1897 registers, 32 LUT-RAM units, five BSRAMs
and two DSPs. The slightly larger transaction with separate guard and
legality flops measured 82.664 MHz and retained 4197447 validated
CoreMark bracket cycles. Full-width transaction payloads, narrower
prediction metadata, smaller hashed tables and one-bit direction
alternatives timed worse and are excluded from this candidate.

The selected prototype also retains exactly 4197447 bracket cycles;
the unchanged validator accepts all canonical CRCs and completion text,
and the run completes at EBREAK, in bounds, with both markers. Verilator
lint passes. All eight retirement cosim comparisons pass for selftest
and random1/random2/random3, each under zero-wait and imem+dmem stalls.
The unchanged formal suite and unit tests remain implementation gates;
no formal pass is claimed for this isolated hypothesis prototype.

approximately 1.78 percent above 194.25. This is below the required

Expected integer fitness gain is 2 percent with medium confidence.

bounds and bracketing, all original tests and formal/cosim gates, and

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change multiplication to a fully pipelined, in-order MEM-available producer.
Launch four DSP-sized partial products directly from the existing finalized
ID/EX operands and registered sign-extension bits. Capture all partials at
the EX/MEM boundary; recombine and select the architectural result only
in MEM. Exclude multiplication from current-EX forwarding and use one
load-style dependency bubble only when the next encoded source matches
its nonzero destination. Independent instructions and independent multiplies
continue issuing every cycle. This is one change to multiplication execution
structure and its necessary dependency interlock.

Decompose each prepared signed 33-bit operand into unsigned low 16 bits
and signed high 17 bits: A=a_lo+(a_hi<<16), B=b_lo+(b_hi<<16).
Compute p00=a_lo*b_lo as unsigned 32 bits; p01=a_lo*b_hi and
p10=a_hi*b_lo as signed 34 bits, explicitly zero-extending each unsigned
low operand to signed 17 bits; p11=a_hi*b_hi is signed 34 bits.
The existing sign flops make MULH signed/signed, MULHSU signed/unsigned,
and MULHU unsigned/unsigned. MUL uses the same decomposition's low half.
There is no full-width native multiplier, unsigned-product sign correction,

title: Bank-local pipelined predictor maintenance with ordered collision forwarding
motivation:
The current 64-entry predictor already removes most branch bubbles.
Accuracy-only additions have insufficient headroom, and recent registered
training and delayed recovery attempts did not clear acceptance. Prior
asynchronous banking changed only target storage. Complete small banks
with registered read-modify-write maintenance offer a different tradeoff:
shorten both lookup selection and the maintenance loop while keeping
resolved EX control out of table write decoding. LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one bank-local pipelined maintenance architecture for the
existing tagged predictor. Preserve all 64 logical entries and PC[7:2]
mapping, using four independent sixteen-row banks. PC[7:6] selects the
bank and PC[5:2] its row. Bank the tags, targets, counters, jump bits and
validity together, rather than banking only target payload. Preserve
twelve-bit tags, eighteen-bit target words, two-bit counters and the
exact original prediction and stale-invalidation policy.

Capture one predecoded forty-bit transaction on each original accepted
EX update edge: validity, PC[19:2], target[19:2], allocate, jump and actual
taken. Validity requires update_en and the full original PC range and
alignment guard. Allocation requires effective legality, branch-or-jump
kind and the full original target range/alignment guard. Check original
full addresses before truncation. Bubbles replace validity with zero;
capture never repeats under memory holds or division waits.

In the following maintenance stage, read only the selected bank's local
tag, counter and jump state, perform exact matching and saturation, and
register a complete commit command: enable, allocate-versus-invalidate,
six-bit index, twelve-bit tag, eighteen-bit target, counter and jump kind.
Table payload writes and validity updates then use only this saved commit
command on the next edge. A transaction accepted on edge N therefore
becomes lookup-visible after edge N+2. Allocation updates every row field
atomically; invalidation clears only validity. A nonallocating tag miss
creates no write. Pending stages drain independently of later EX/MEM
readiness; there is one transaction per edge and no queue interlock.

Forward the pending commit row into maintenance when its index equals
the transaction being processed. Allocation forwards valid/tag/counter/
jump; invalidation forwards valid=0. Compare the forwarded tag with the
transaction tag before counter reuse. This is essential for consecutive
same-PC training, conflicting-tag replacement, kind changes and stale
invalidation: maintenance must see the most recent older logical row,
including the command committing on that edge. Do not forward pending
commands into fetch lookup. Conditional replacements start weak from
actual outcome; matching conditional counters saturate; jump-to-branch
changes start weak; jumps remain unconditional and replace actual targets.
Not-taken branches still train their direct destination, never PC+4.

Lookup remains asynchronous and PC-only. Each bank reads its sixteen-row
payload, compares the original tag and validity, and qualifies its output
with bank selection and the full lookup guard. Combine the four qualified
target words and direction bits with balanced reductions. A matching
not-taken row still exposes its stored target; misses produce zeros.
Payloads remain unreset and validity alone guards their visibility.
Reset clears all bank validity and both pending-stage valid/enables,
cancels queued work, and suppresses writes. Lookup acceptance on a commit
edge sees the old row and saves that exact prediction with the instruction.

Keep the instruction pipeline, finalized operand forwarding, immediate
accepted EX recovery, full-width target resolution, saved prediction
metadata and all architectural trap/link/PC behavior unchanged. Predictor
state is advisory; extra training latency can add cold misses but cannot
change execution. Preserve stale ordinary/illegal-hit repair, changing
JALR targets, misalignment suppression, recovery priority, held operands,
sticky division and wrong-path side-effect killing. Preserve nret=1 and
top-level IO, decoder defaults, true/ALTOPS arithmetic, all memory and RVFI
invariants, progress, bounds, canonical CRCs and marker bracketing.

combined bank-local pipeline, which has not been measured. Isolated full
flop replacement, complete asynchronous banking and early comparison
leaves regressed in this investigation and are excluded. An unbanked
two-stage maintenance prototype measured median 77.845 MHz and therefore
does not establish a gain. The proposed bank-local version must earn its
improvement by shortening maintenance selection and write routing; extra
distributed memory, collision forwarding, cold misses and residual ALU/
ID paths may erase it. Do not claim an acceptance win from these estimates.
Measure actual canonical stalled CoreMark cycles and median Gowin Fmax;
fitness must exceed 203.1855 iter/sec. At 4197447 cycles this requires
approximately 85.29 MHz. All unchanged correctness gates remain required.

implementation_notes:
# Bank-local pipelined predictor maintenance

Implemented four independent sixteen-row banks for validity, twelve-bit tags,
eighteen-bit target words, two-bit counters and jump kind. The logical index is
unchanged: PC[7:6] selects the bank and PC[5:2] selects the row.

Accepted EX updates capture exactly forty bits: validity, PC[19:2], target[19:2],
allocation, jump and actual taken. Full thirty-two-bit PC and target range and
alignment guards are checked before truncation. Maintenance reads each bank's
local state and qualifies the selected result, forwarding the older saved commit
on an exact six-bit index collision. Forwarded validity and tag are checked before
counter reuse. A complete forty-one-bit command commits on edge N+2 for a
transaction accepted on edge N. Both stages advance on every clock independently
of later memory/division holds, and reset cancels both stages and suppresses writes.

Allocation atomically writes every row field; stale repair clears only validity.
Nonallocating tag misses create no command. Fetch remains asynchronous and PC-only,
with four qualified bank outputs combined by balanced reductions. It sees table
contents only, including the old row on a commit acceptance edge. Not-taken hits
expose their stored direct targets. Payloads remain unreset.

Only branch_predictor.sv and its two cocotb test files changed. The instruction
pipeline, operand forwarding, immediate EX recovery, full-width resolution, nret=1
IO, arithmetic, memory and RVFI logic are unchanged. The only implementation
refinement from the initial structure is that saved commit metadata comes directly
from the captured transaction; only enable and trained counter require bank-result
reductions. This avoids routing maintenance-dependent selection through every
metadata bit without changing the command or latency.

Tests retain original policy and architectural assertions, updating only the
prediction/redirect expectations that depended on immediate table visibility.
An independent model applies the original policy in acceptance order and publishes
results exactly two edges later. Coverage includes continuous same-PC saturation,
conflicting tags, all banks and rows, kind changes, stale invalidation, disabled
inputs, full-address guards, direct not-taken targets, once-only commands and drain,
pre/post-commit lookup collisions, exact saved instruction predictions, pending
reset and payload preservation across invalidation/reset. Pipeline tests check
pending maintenance draining during later memory/division holds and reset with
two pending controls, while preserving PC/link/operands/order and side-effect checks.

Local verification:

- Requested warning-clean Verilator lint: PASS.
- Full cocotb suite: PASS (seven pytest runners, including true and ALTOPS ALU).
  The final predictor/pipeline rerun and explicit commit/fetch collision assertion
  also passed (six predictor tests and thirty-six pipeline tests).
- Formal with RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 and the original
  formal/run_all.sh: PASS, 53 checks, zero failures, no failure fix attempts.
  The final rerun after restoring the best measured implementation also passed
  all 53 checks.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: PASS for selftest with and without stalls and
  canonical stalled CoreMark CRC validation. Final restored RTL also passed.
- Canonical Gowin/CoreMark fitness was measured with NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench.

Measurements (all runs: 4,197,447 marker-bracketed stalled cycles, ten iterations):

| Implementation | Gowin placement 0/1/2 MHz | Median MHz | Iterations/sec |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initially masked complete bank commands | 70.619 / 71.215 / 71.215 | 71.215 | 169.66 |
| Direct saved metadata, retained implementation | 73.058 / 77.674 / 77.674 | 77.674 | 185.05 |
| Factored tag matching and Boolean saturation, reverted | 70.811 / 75.428 / 75.428 | 75.428 | 179.70 |

The retained implementation uses 4,789 Gowin logic cells, 1,938 registers,
52 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its reported critical path has eleven logic
levels and crosses EX/ID operand/result selection into the multiplier input
register. Repeating the full FPGA fitness measurement after restoration reproduced
all three placement frequencies, the 4,197,447-cycle count and 185.05 fitness.

The hypothesis does not meet the required fitness threshold of 203.1855

cycle count it would need more than 85.28604 MHz median Fmax. No acceptance win or
estimated six-percent gain is claimed. Additional training latency and residual
EX/ID paths prevent this measured implementation from establishing an improvement.

Correct the old-row collision with a small last-committed-row register.
Record every actual table write: present, six-bit index, resulting
validity, twelve-bit tag, two-bit counter and jump kind. An allocation

title: Decouple fetch from backend holds with a two-entry fall-through queue
motivation:
The champion scores 194.25 iter/sec at 81.537 MHz with 4,197,447
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Fetch currently stops on every
load-use, data-memory and divider hold, losing opportunities to collect
instructions while the independent instruction bus is ready. The

title: Prepare direct BTB allocation with bounded 22-bit eligibility arithmetic
motivation:
The champion scores 194.25 iterations/sec at 81.537 MHz with 4,197,447
timed CoreMark cycles. Predictor experiments repeatedly expose paths from
branch resolution through predictor maintenance into ID or validity clock
enables. The original allocation gate consumes effective EX legality,
whose conditional-branch misalignment term depends on the late branch
outcome, despite allocation independently rejecting every misaligned
target. A local one-bit direction prototype passed retirement cosim and
CRC validation but scored only 74.114 MHz in placement option zero; its
worst path still ended at predictor validity enable. Changing direction
accuracy therefore did not remove the relevant allocation dependency.
LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Prepare only the eligibility of direct control-flow allocations at the
existing ID/EX boundary. Add one predictor_direct_ok bit to id_ex_t.
In ID first qualify the original fetch PC as lower-1-MiB and word
aligned. For prediction-maintenance eligibility only, form a signed
22-bit sum of {2'b00, fetch_PC[19:0]} and the decoded B/J immediate
sign-extended to 22 bits. Set the bit exactly for a validated legal
conditional branch or JAL, excluding JALR, with the full PC guard true,
sum[21:20] equal to zero and sum[1:0] equal to zero. Capture this bit with its
instruction; clear it on reset, flush or bubble and retain it on every
existing hold. Do not register the candidate target word or use this
temporary sum for architectural execution.

In EX expose the registered direct-control kind and this captured
eligibility bit to branch_predictor alongside the original accepted
update transaction. For a direct branch/JAL, use the saved bit as the
predictor allocation qualifier instead of recomputing effective legality
and representability from live EX resolution. Continue to qualify the
update itself with original ex_accept and full update-PC range/alignment.
For JALR retain the original effective-legality, jump-kind and full
resolved-target range/alignment checks, because its target depends on
finalized rs1. Ordinary instructions use the original matching-only stale
invalidation path. An ineligible direct update also retains that exact
invalidation behavior. Full PC guards must authorize the bounded sum;
full EX target guards remain authoritative for indirect updates. A B/J
immediate is at most a signed 21-bit value, so a lower-1-MiB PC plus its
offset lies in [-1,048,576, 2,097,149], fitting signed 22 bits exactly.
Thus sum[21:20]==0 recognizes exactly the representable direct targets,
without truncation wraparound or a full 32-bit adder/high-bit reduction.

This preserves every table transition: an aligned representable direct
target cannot raise the EX branch/jump misalignment fault, so allocation
depends solely on decoded legality and the precomputed target guard.
An unrepresentable or misaligned direct target cannot allocate regardless
of the branch outcome and still invalidates only its matching row.
Actual taken/not-taken remains the original resolved outcome and trains
the unchanged two-bit saturating counter once per EX acceptance. Tags,
targets, jump bits and validity still write atomically on the original
edge; fetch still sees old rows on a simultaneous lookup/update edge.

The intended timing gain is removing actual_taken-to-effective-trap
qualification from high-fanout direct BTB write/validity controls.
Payload targets still come from the original full EX PC+immediate adder.
The explicitly bounded ID sum feeds only one eligibility flop. Preserve
full 32-bit architectural execution and RVFI addresses; the temporary
bounded sum can authorize only predictor maintenance. Unlike r8s2, which registered both the full
direct target and its eligibility and regressed to 71.732 MHz, this
proposal adds only one bit and retains the original EX target datapath.
Unlike r9s0, it does not rewrite producer forwarding enables or substitute
a live EX allocation predicate. No change to predictor capacity, banking,
indexing, direction policy, training edge, lookup, recovery latency,
arithmetic, forwarding or pipeline depth belongs in this proposal.

Preserve original full-width architectural branch/JAL/JALR resolution,
legality/misalignment traps and RVFI next PCs, immediate mismatch recovery,
wrong-path suppression, acceptance and imem/load-use/dmem/division holds.
Preserve nret=1, exact top-level memory and channel-0 RVFI ports,
retirement order/progress, real RV32IM and ALTOPS results, decoder defaults,
memory bounds, canonical CoreMark CRCs and timing markers. The eligibility
bit authorizes predictor maintenance only and never changes a trap,
redirect destination, architectural memory operation or retirement.

A wide 32-bit eligibility-only prototype passed lint and preserved all
4,197,447 canonical stalled CoreMark cycles, but measured median Fmax of
77.143 MHz and therefore regressed. The final proposed refinement uses
the proven bounded 22-bit eligibility arithmetic and full PC guards;
it has not been scored. Do not reuse the wide prototype timing as a
claimed result for this different circuit. Estimate seven percent fitness
improvement with low confidence. Even the bounded ID eligibility adder
or remaining indirect-update paths may dominate.
Require actual canonical stalled CoreMark cycles times median Gowin Fmax
above 203.1855 iterations/sec; at unchanged 4,197,447 cycles this requires
more than 85.288 MHz. A single placement or circuit-neutral timing shift
does not establish acceptance. Run unchanged architectural/formal/cosim
and CRC gates, and explicitly check equivalence of direct allocation
and matching stale invalidation against the original predictor.
